title: RAD-PHI2: Instruction Tuning PHI-2 for Radiology
authors: Mercy Ranjit, Gopinath Ganapathy, Shaury Srivastav, Tanuja Ganu, Srujana Oruganti
text:
Recent advances in natural language processing (NLP) have enabled the development of powerful language models that can generate natural language texts for various purposes and domains. However, most of the existing language models are trained on general domain texts, such as news articles, books, web pages, etc., and may not be able to handle the specific vocabulary, concepts, terminology, and style of radiology texts. Hence, it is required to have domain specific models that embody knowledge for that domain and trained for specific tasks in domain specific workflows to deal with the nuances of the field. But, the size and complexity of these language models are often prohibitive for practical applications, as they require a large amount of computational resources and memory to train and run.

In this paper, we explore the use of small language models (SLMs) for radiology related tasks, specifically text-related tasks relating to radiology knowledge and tasks that are useful in everyday radiology workflows pertaining to radiology reports.

SLMs are language models that have a relatively small number of parameters, compared to the state-of-the-art large language models, such as GPT-4 [1]. SLMs, specifically Phi-2 [2] is a 2.7 billion parameter model that has shown remarkable performance in general domain language understanding, reasoning, and coding tasks, but its capabilities in the medical domain, especially on radiology content and tasks specific to a radiology workflows is not explored. Moreover, Phi-2 is not an instruction tuned model and tends to produce verbose answers as it was trained from synthetic text books and currently not suitable for direct deployments in application workflows to perform specific tasks. We hypothesize that SLMs can be effectively adapted to the radiology domain by finetuning them on high-quality radiology content to bring-in the nuanced radiology knowledge and also be adapted to perform specific tasks that are useful in everyday radiology workflows. SLMs provide the advantage of having a domain specific model for easy consumption at lower computational cost and faster inference.

The Phi models [2] success and its on-par performance to large language models was attributed to the high quality aka “textbook-quality" training data that was used for its training. The training corpus was augmented with carefully selected data, filtered based on educational value and content quality. It demonstrated that this choice of training data enabled Phi-2 to achieve outstanding performance on complex benchmarks, matching or outperforming models up to 25x larger in size. We extend this approach of Phi-2 by using high-quality and reliable educational content from Radiopaedia [3] to finetune Phi-2 for radiology knowledge. Radiopaedia is a rapidly growing collaborative online peer-reviewed open-edit radiology resource, compiled by radiologists and other health professionals from across the globe. Training from this highly valuable and reliable source can embody the model with this knowledge making it useful to answer questions on radiology accurately. To test our hypothesis, we use Phi-2, a 2.7 billion parameter SLM, as our base model, and finetune it on question-answer pairs derived from the educational articles of Radiopaedia pertaining to different systems like chest, cardiac, gastrointestinal etc. The resulting model Rad-Phi2 Base, can answer queries on radiology pertaining to these systems accurately. We evaluate the performance of Rad-Phi2-Base and compare it with larger instruction tuned models, such as Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 [4] which was finetuned on the same radiology question answer pairs and also GPT-4. Rad-Phi2 Base performs better than or comparable to the much larger counterparts while producing more crisp and to-the-point answers. It even surpassed the Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) approach [5] that directly used a knowledge base of Radiopaedia articles to answer the queries.

Apart from answering queries on radiology, there are specific text-related tasks that can be useful in AI deployment scenarios of radiology workflows. Some useful tasks relating to radiology reporting workflows are writing diagnostic impression summary from radiology findings, tagging of radiology reports with appropriate abnormality labels to flag priority cases, noise free extraction of findings and impression from existing radiology reports, generating a comparison summary of findings between the current radiology report and its prior report etc. Some of these tasks were also cited in the earlier work [6] in the context of application of language models in radiology workflows. To address these useful tasks that arise in the AI deployment scenarios of radiology workflows, we create an instruction tuning dataset for tasks pertaining to radiology reports of Chest X-rays and instruction-tune Phi-2 and obtain the Rad-Phi2 model. But, as Phi-2 was not an instruction tuned model in the first place, we first instruction tune Phi-2 for general domain tasks using the Super Natural instruction tuning dataset [7]. The resulting model Phi2-Instruct(SupNatInst) is then further instruction tuned for tasks specific to radiology reports. The resulting model, Rad-Phi2 can perform specific tasks that are useful in AI driven radiology reporting workflows of Chest X-rays. Our results show that Rad-Phi2 performs better or on-par with a larger model like Mistral-7B-Instruct(v0.2) finetuned on the same instruction tuning dataset.

We would also like to note that while GPT-4 has reasonable radiology knowledge as noted in this work [8], it still falls short on nuanced tasks like impression generation in comparison to domain specific models unless given with a large number of carefully curated examples in conjunction with sophisticated prompt engineering approaches [9]. SLMs enables to develop domain-specific models for these nuanced task types easily and quickly due to the low resource requirements associated with its size.

Our work demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of using SLMs for radiology specific tasks, and opens up new possibilities for improving the quality and efficiency of radiology practice.

Our key Contributions include:

- • We demonstrate the effectiveness of SLMs in the radiology domain by training on high quality radiology content from Radiopaedia [3]. The resulting model Rad-Phi2-Base can answer general queries on radiology like symptoms, radiological appearances of findings, differential diagnosis, prognosis, and treatments w.r.t diseases pertaining to 15 different systems like Chest, Cardiac etc. It performs better than larger models like Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 finetuned on the same dataset. It also performed better than GPT-4 and the Retrieval Augmented Generation approach that directly used Radiopaedia content as the knowledge source while answering queries.

- • We construct an instruction tuning dataset of text related tasks that are useful in radiology report writing workflows of Chest X-rays using GPT-4 processing and annotations of existing datasets on Chest X-ray reports. We share the prompts for different tasks used in creating this dataset.

- • We also demonstrate Instruction Tuning on SLMs to make it usable for practical tasks involved in radiology workflows. As Phi-2 is not an instruction tuned model and tends to produce verbose answers, we first perform general domain instruction tuning using the Super Natural Instructions dataset followed by radiology specific instruction tuning on tasks related to radiology reports of Chest X-rays. We call the resulting model Rad-Phi2 which is useful in performing everyday tasks in radiology report writing workflows of Chest X-rays.

- • Our ablation studies gives insights on the input formats that worked the best when instruction tuning the Phi-2 model. We note that radiology specific instruction tuning performs better when preceded by general domain instruction tuning and semantic tasks like Natural Language Inference(NLI) can help with the performance of other tasks.
